questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “ESP32 family and board selection”?
options: Start with the official `hello_world` example and record the working toolchain version.
ESP32 family members do not all have the same radios and peripherals.
Pin selection must be checked against the exact module and board schematic.
ESP-IDF selects the chip target before building.
questions.answer: ESP32 family members do not all have the same radios and peripherals.
questions.explanation:
ESP32 family members do not all have the same radios and peripherals.
Why: ESP32, S2, S3, C2/C3/C6, and H2 variants differ in CPU, radio, USB, and peripherals. Check the exact module datasheet, board schematic, and framework support before choosing.

Origin and date: Espressif Systems developed the ESP32 family, and the first ESP32 chip was introduced in 2016. The goal was to combine Wi‑Fi and Bluetooth in one MCU, reducing the cost and complexity of separate radio and processor components. ESP32 boards power sensor nodes, smart devices, gateways, and low-cost IoT products; they connect to careers in embedded firmware, IoT platforms, radio testing, and power optimization. If small, energy-aware devices that move sensor readings to network services inspire you, learn to choose the exact ESP32 variant before designing.

The additional `idf.py` commands configure and build an ESP-IDF project only. They have no direct Arduino-sketch equivalent; Arduino-ESP32 selects a board package and builds sketches with Arduino IDE/CLI.
